 Coram : Sharmila U. Deshmukh, J.
 Date : 8th April, 2025.
 Oral Judgment :
 1.

The First Appeal has been preferred against the judgment and  Award dated 18th June, 2019 passed by the Reference Court in L.A.R.
 No. 556 of 2008 filed by the original Claimants under Section 18 of the  Land Acquisition Act, 1894 [for short, "L. A. Act"].
The Reference came  to be dismissed by the Reference Court as the Claimants remained  absent and did not lead any evidence in Court.

2. Learned counsel appearing for Appellant submits that as per the  settled position in law, it is not permissible for the Reference Court to  dismiss the reference for non-prosecution and though the issues were  framed and answered by the Reference Court, the same is not an  Award on merits in as much as neither the Claimants nor the  Respondent-Land Acquisition Officer led any evidence and in the  absence of any evidence being led, the Land Reference could not have  been dismissed and without any evidence being led, the issues could  Sairaj 2 of 6 Mr. Ravji Punja Bodke Since Deceased ... vs State Of Maharshtra Through Special ... on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24869535/

3.

sentences.text: Per contra, Mr. Sonavane, learned AGP submits that the burden was upon the Claimants to establish that the compensation awarded by the Special Land Acquisition Officer was grossly inadequate and the burden has not been discharged as the Claimants remained absent and did not file any evidence on record.
He submits that State cannot be saddled with the burden of payment of interest for default on the part of the Claimants.

4. In Rejoinder, learned counsel appearing for Appellants would rely upon the decision in the case of Chandaba w/o. Gangaram Pauyed vs. The State of Maharashtra1 where this Court after considering various decisions on the subject has held that the Reference has to be decided on merits by the Civil Court on the basis of material before it.

entities.text: Chandaba w/o. Gangaram Pauyed vs. The State of Maharashtra1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He would submit that the facts of the said case are identical to the facts in the present case and the Award which is passed by the Reference Court cannot be held to be an 'Award' within the meaning of Section 26 of the L. A. Act.
5. I have considered the submissions and perused the record.

6. The only issue which would arise for consideration is whether the impugned judgment constitutes 'Award' within the meaning of Section 26 of the L. A. Act and the issue as far as adequacy of compensation 1 2023 (2) ALL MR 307.

7. Perusal of the impugned judgment would indicate that necessary issues were framed by Reference Court and thereafter, it records that the Claimants have not led any evidence nor remained present before the Trial Court.

The Reference Court has further taken into consideration the copy of Award, notices issued under Section 12(2) of the L. A. Act, 7/12 extracts of the acquired land and Kabje Pavti of the acquired land and has thereafter held that as no evidence has been led on behalf of the Claimants, the documentary evidence is not sufficient to prove the Reference Application filed by the Claimants.
Perusal of the impugned judgment does not demonstrate that any evidence was led by the Special Land Acquisition Officer.

As the Award of Land Acquisition Officer was merely an offer, it was necessary for the Land Acquisition Officer to step into the box and lead evidence in order to demonstrate the adequacy of compensation.

8. In the decision of Chandaba w/o. Gangaram Pauyed (supra), this Court in the identical facts had held that considering the form the Award has to take as specified under Section 26 of the L. A. Act, the Award passed by the Reference Court is not an 'Award' within a meaning of Section 26 of L. A. Act.

9. The facts of the present case are identical and it is evident from the impugned judgment and Award that the Reference has been Mr. Ravji Punja Bodke Since Deceased ... vs State Of Maharshtra Through Special ...

10.
In light of above, the impugned judgment cannot be sustained.
However, at the same time, the State cannot be saddled with the payment of interest on the account of default on the part of Claimants having not led evidence.

It is, therefore, necessary that the matter be remanded to the Reference Court to be decided afresh, however,
subject to the condition that the Claimants will not be entitled to interest from the date of dismissal of the Land Acquisition Reference till the final disposal of the Land Acquisition Reference by the Reference Court, on the enhanced compensation, if any, by the Reference Court.
11.
In light of the above, the following order is passed:-

:ORDER:
[i] The impugned Award dated 18th June, 2019 passed by the Court of Civil Judge, Senior Division,
Nashik in Land Acquisition Reference No. 556 of 2008 is hereby quashed and set aside and Land Acquisition Reference is restored to the original position.
[ii] The Parties to appear before the Reference Court on 7 th May, 2025.
[iii] The Reference Court will permit the parties to lead oral and documentary evidence in support of their respective Sairaj 5 of 6 119 FA-352-2020.doc contentions.
[iv] The concerned Reference Court shall dispose of Land Acquisition Reference as expeditiously as possible.
